subject: Post-call: p95/p99 SLO playbook & next steps (OrchidHealth)
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@orchidhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — quick clarifications on p95/p99 targets

Hannah / Ben — thanks again for the demo this morning. High level the team liked the hosted latency profile, but we need to make sure the numbers map to our real traffic shape before we move to a POC. A few clarifications we need for the next run: 

- Can you confirm how p95/p99 are computed end-to-end (client -> your gateway -> model -> return)? Do you include network egress to our region?
- We run a mix of short chat turn (avg 18 tokens) and long generation (>500 tokens) workflows. How do you recommend we weight those in your simulated profile?
- Streaming: for the chat path we stream partial tokens; we need to guarantee time-to-first-byte p95 within 150ms for short-turns at 1000 rps. Is that feasible on hosted?

Can you send a short playbook / checklist we can review internally — include throughput, concurrency, and any client-side backpressure guidance.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Platform Engineering
OrchidHealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick clarifications on p95/p99 targets

Sarah — appreciate the clear asks. Recap of our post-call alignment and what we'll deliver by Friday: 

1) Definition: Our p95/p99 numbers will reflect end-to-end server-side latency from when your request hits our public API endpoint to the final token emitted by the model service (server-side RTT). Network transit between your clients and your edge (e.g., mobile network) is not included. We will, however, provide region egress measurements (API start -> your VPC) if you want to account for last-mile separately.

2) Workload mix: We'll generate a composite profile with two buckets — "chat short-turns" (avg 18 tokens, median seq len 24) and "long-gen" (avg 520 tokens). We'll run weighted blends at 80/20 and 60/40 to mirror your prod signals; please confirm preferred split and peak RPS target.

3) Streaming guarantees: For hosted streaming we can target time-to-first-byte (TTFB) p95 <= 150ms for short-turns at up to 1k rps with the following constraints:
   - Use HTTP/2 streaming with SSE fallback for older clients
   - Keep concurrency per connection <= 8 to avoid head-of-line delays
   - Enable per-request KV caching for repeated prefixes (we'll suggest cache keys)

4) Throughput & concurrency guidance: We'll propose instance sizing and batch settings for a 1k rps peak with expected concurrency envelope. Marcus will attach simulated traces and config snippets for your infra team.

Next steps (we'll action):
- Friday EOD: Draft SLO playbook (PDF) + simulated trace CSV + hosted config snippets (Ben/Marcus)
- Monday: Quick call to review playbook and agree test schedule (you pick 30-min window)

If that works, we'll iterate. Attaching an initial draft playbook and a small trace sample.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0139

Attachment: orchid_slo_playbook_draft.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@orchidhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: p95/p99 SLO playbook & next steps (OrchidHealth)

Sarah — adding technical detail and the simulated traces as promised. Key notes below and attached config snippets.

- How we compute p95/p99: We sample per-request server timestamps at ingress (api gateway) and model emit completion and calculate the delta; streaming is measured as time-to-first-byte for the initial partial chunk and time-to-last-byte for completion. We include queuing time inside the serving runtime.
- For your short-turn TTFB p95 <= 150ms at 1k rps: our hosted cluster in us-west-2 hit 140ms p95 with continuous batching disabled (concurrency-targeted mode) in internal tests. The attached CSV includes a representative trace set and a runbook for toggling batching on/off.
- Concurrency guidance: start with 6–8 concurrent inflight requests per connection for chat clients, and cap client-side retries to exponential backoff starting at 50ms. Server-side max concurrency per worker should be 32 for 1k rps profile.
- Failure / fallback: we'll propose a fallback to a lower-cost model variant when we observe sustained p99 > SLA for >15 mins and provide automatic routing policies.

Attachments included: p95p99-simulated-trace-sample.csv, redwood-hosted-config-snippets.txt

Ben Carter
Staff Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@orchidhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: p95/p99 SLO playbook & next steps (OrchidHealth)

Hannah / Ben — thanks for the thorough packet. Quick confirmation from our side:

- We'll review the playbook and simulated traces today.
- Preference for workload split: start with 80% short-turn / 20% long-gen for initial runs, ramp to 1k rps.
- Monday 9/13 10:00 PT works for a 30-min sync to walk through the playbook and the go/no-go criteria for the POC.

One ask: can you include a short checklist of measurable acceptance criteria that our SRE team can use during the POC (e.g., p95 TTFB target, p99 completion target, allowable error-rate threshold)? If you can embed that in the final playbook we'll be ready to sign off on scheduling the POC.

Thanks,
Tom Alvarez
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
OrchidHealth
